text: # CHAPTER 3 - CLASSES *In the dimly lit courtyard of the ancient monastery, moonlight filtered through the cherry blossom trees, casting a haunting glow upon the scene. Zhang, the seasoned warrior monk, stood with unwavering resolve, his martial robes fluttering gently in the night breeze. Across from him, Tanaka, an ancient monastic vampire, exuded an eerie aura, his crimson eyes gleaming with centuries of malevolent knowledge. The battle between these two formidable opponents was a clash of philosophies and life forces. Zhang, guided by his unwavering dedication to the path of enlightenment, represented the essence of discipline and self-control. Tanaka, on the other hand, embodied the darker side of monastic teachings, having succumbed to the allure of immortality at a great cost.* *As the first strikes were exchanged, the clash of their combat styles filled the air with an electric tension. Zhang's movements were precise and deliberate, his attacks a seamless dance of precision and grace. He moved with the fluidity of water, responding to each of Tanaka's deadly strikes with a calm, centred presence.* *Tanaka, a creature sustained by unholy power, possessed unnatural strength and agility. His attacks were swift and brutal, a dark reflection of the once-noble techniques he had mastered as a monk. With every blow, Zhang felt the corrupting influence of Tanaka's vampiric nature, threatening to weaken his resolve.* *The battle raged on through the night, each combatant drawing upon their inner strength and training. Zhang's resolve was unshaken, his spirit fuelled by the monastery's teachings of balance and harmony. In contrast, Tanaka's centuries of experience lent him an air of cunning and unpredictability.* *As the first light of dawn began to creep over the horizon, Zhang knew that time was running out. The vampire, weakened by the approaching sun, grew increasingly desperate. In one final, desperate lunge, Tanaka launched himself at Zhang, fangs bared.* *With a swift, precise strike, Zhang channelled the full force of his inner chi into a single blow. His palm connected with Tanaka's chest, and a blinding burst of light erupted from the point of impact. The ancient vampire let out a haunting scream as he was engulfed in the purifying energy of Zhang's strike.* *As the sunlight bathed the courtyard, Tanaka disintegrated into a cloud of ash, his malevolent existence brought to an end. Zhang, victorious but weary, stood alone amidst the blossoms, a testament to the enduring power of the monastic teachings that had guided him on his path.* ## CLASSES The five new character classes found in this supplement are the Disciple, Ghostwalker, Kensai, Mystic and Oathblade. These classes make extensive use of techniques with the Focus trait, while the Mystic and several character options also gain innate spells. Focus is a recharge mechanic rather than a separate source of power, and all magic granted by these classes follows the normal innate spell rules unless stated otherwise. The layout of each character class follows the same format as found in the TRG Core Rulebook and is briefly summarised here. **CLASS TYPE** Each character class belongs to one of three categories. These categories are Adept, Expert and Martial. **DESCRIPTION** A brief description explaining what your class’s main purpose is and what its strengths are. Also included is an indication as to what role the class can play in a party of adventurers. **KEY ABILITY SCORES** These are the most commonly helpful ability scores for this class and also one ability score has a minimum requirement. **PROFICIENCIES** Gives the armour and weapons that the class is trained to use. You may expand upon these by selecting feats and may gain additional proficiencies from race and other options. **CLASS SKILLS** Your class will have a number of skills which gain a special bonus type called a class bonus. Your class bonus is determined by your class level. **SKILL POINTS** This is how many skill points you have to spend on skills each level. You may develop a maximum of 1 rank per level in any skill. **HIT POINTS** This entry will tell you how many hit points your character gains each time you take a level in the class. You also gain an additional amount of hit points each level equal to your Con hp mod and any racial modifiers. **CLASS ABILITIES** Your class will have access to a number of unique special abilities which will be explained here. MAGICAL TRADITION Where these classes gain magic, it is handled using the innate spell rules from the TRG Core Rulebook. The Focus trait only determines when an ability becomes expended and how it can be restored. **CLASS SUMMARY TABLE** Each class also has a class table which shows its key statistical information. ## DISCIPLE **CLASS TYPE** Martial **DESCRIPTION** For you, martial skill transcends the battlefield it is a lifestyle, a doctrine, and a state of mind. You search out methods of battle beyond swords and shields, finding weapons within themselves just as capable of crippling or killing as any blade. You elevate your body to be-come a weapon of war, from battle-minded ascetic to self-taught brawler. You tread the path of discipline, to discover within yourself not what you are, but what you are meant to be. You excel at overcoming even the most daunting perils, striking where it’s least expected, and taking advantage of enemy vulnerabilities. Fleet of foot and skilled in combat, you can navigate any battlefield with ease, aiding allies wherever you are needed most. **KEY ABILITY SCORES** Wisdom (min +2), Dexterity, Strength **PROFICIENCIES** You may use all simple weapons and any weapons that have the monastic trait (see chapter 6). **CLASS SKILLS** Acrobatics, Artistry, Athletics, Climbing, Culture, Meditation, Mental Focus, Perception, Sense Motive, Stealth **SKILL POINTS** 6 + Int per level **HIT POINTS** 10 + Con per level **CLASS ABILITIES** You gain the following abilities as a Disciple as you advance in levels. POWERFUL FISTS You know how to wield your fists as deadly weapons. The damage of your unarmed attacks is1d6 rather than the usual 1d4 inflicted by an unarmed attack. Additionally, your unarmed attacks gain the versatile bludgeoning trait. As you become more experienced, the amount of damage that you inflict with your unarmed strikes also increases. When your BAB becomes 3 and for every 3 it increases thereafter you inflict an additional point of total unarmed damage. Be aware that this is total unarmed damage and not base. Your base damage die still increase in the usual way. Finally, your unarmed strikes also gain the ability to overcome various damage types as your combat prowess increases. When your BAB reaches 3, your strikes class as magical. When your BAB reaches 8 your unarmed strikes are treated as cold iron and silver and at BAB 16 they are treated as adamantine. **DISCIPLES DODGE** At 1st level you may add your Wisdom ability score as a dodge bonus to your Defence (DB). This bonus is only applied if you are unencumbered and wearing no armour. **DISCIPLES** RESOLVE Your training has served you well and gives you that slight edge over others. You may increase your conviction pool and conviction points by 1. **FLURRY OF BLOWS** **FLOURISH** **Action** 1 AP Make two unarmed Strikes. If both hit the same creature, apply DR, resistance and weakness only once. Apply your multiple attack penalty to the Strikes normally. Be aware that you may only inflict one critical injury when using this ability, although you still gain additional critical damage from both strikes. **BONUS FEATS** You gain the Inner Discipline feat and may select any one additional class feat with the Technique trait. At 3rd level and then every 3 levels thereafter you may select an additional class feat. This class feat must be one for which you meet the prerequisites or match the appropriate class trait (Martial or Disciple). **DEEP FOCUS** Your training allows you to sustain the concentration required for your techniques longer than others. Each technique you possess with the Focus trait can be used one additional time before it becomes expended and must be restored with Refocus (Mental Focus). Each technique tracks its uses separately. When you successfully Refocus a technique, all of the uses granted to that technique by Deep Focus are restored. MONASTIC PATH As a Disciple you must select one of the Monastic Paths detailed at the end of this chapter. Your Monastic Path determines the magical tradition and magical ability score used by any innate spells or explicitly magical techniques you gain through Inner Tempest, and also grants you a class skill. INCREDIBLE MOVEMENT At 4th level you learn to move like the wind. You gain a +10-foot status bonus to your Speed whenever you’re not wearing armour. The bonus increases by 5 feet at 10th level and every 6 levels thereafter. MAGICAL TRADITION You do not gain a normal spellcasting progression. Your Monastic Path determines the magical tradition and magical ability score of any innate spells or magical techniques you gain from Disciple abilities or feats. | **DISCIPLE TABLE** | | | | | | | |--------------------|---------|---------|----------|---------|----------|-----------------| | Level | **BAB** | **BDB** | **Fort** | **Ref** | **Will** | **Bonus Feats** | | 1st | 1 | 1 | 3 | 6 | 3 | 1 | | 2nd | 2 | 2 | 4 | 7 | 4 | 1 | | 3rd | 3 | 3 | 5 | 8 | 5 | 2 | | 4th | 4 | 4 | 6 | 9 | 6 | 2 | | 5th | 5 | 5 | 7 | 10 | 7 | 2 | | 6th | 6 | 6 | 8 | 11 | 8 | 3 | | 7th | 7 | 7 | 9 | 12 | 9 | 3 | | 8th | 8 | 8 | 10 | 13 | 10 | 3 | | 9th | 9 | 9 | 11 | 14 | 11 | 4 | | 10th | 10 | 10 | 12 | 15 | 12 | 4 | | 11th | 11 | 11 | 13 | 16 | 13 | 4 | | 12th | 12 | 12 | 14 | 17 | 14 | 5 | | 13th | 13 | 13 | 15 | 18 | 15 | 5 | | 14th | 14 | 14 | 16 | 19 | 16 | 5 | | 15th | 15 | 15 | 17 | 20 | 17 | 6 | | 16th | 16 | 16 | 18 | 21 | 18 | 6 | | 17th | 17 | 17 | 19 | 22 | 19 | 6 | | 18th | 18 | 18 | 20 | 23 | 20 | 7 | | 19th | 19 | 19 | 21 | 24 | 21 | 7 | | 20th | 20 | 20 | 22 | 25 | 22 | 7 | ## GHOSTWALKER CLASS TYPE Expert DESCRIPTION You have learned that the most dangerous warrior is not always the strongest, but the one whose presence is not recognised until the killing blow has already fallen. Ghostwalkers are masters of infiltration, misdirection and sudden violence. They train themselves to move without drawing the eye, to control their breathing and footfall, and to exploit the smallest lapse in an opponent’s attention. Some serve as scouts, spies or saboteurs, while others become bodyguards, assassins, thieves or agents trusted to enter places where an army could never tread. Unlike Rogues, who rely upon versatility and opportunism, Ghostwalkers practise a specialised discipline of concealment and movement. They create their own openings, vanish before retaliation can find them and use unusual techniques collectively known as Ghost Arts. Some Ghost Arts are entirely mundane: smoke, concealed weapons, climbing techniques and precise movement. Others cross into the supernatural, allowing experienced Ghostwalkers to fade from sight or pass between shadows. You may want to play a Ghostwalker if you want to infiltrate guarded locations, move rapidly through dangerous terrain, deceive enemies and deliver deadly attacks before disappearing again. KEY ABILITY SCORES Dexterity (min +2), Wisdom, Intelligence PROFICIENCIES You are proficient with light armour and bucklers. You may use all simple weapons, shortbows and weapons with the Monastic trait. The wakizashi is considered a martial weapon for you rather than an exotic weapon. CLASS SKILLS Acrobatics, Athletics, Climbing, Crafting, Culture, Deception, Linguistics, Mental Focus, Perception, Sense Motive, Stealth, Survival, Thievery SKILL POINTS 8 + Int per level HIT POINTS 8 + Con per level **CLASS ABILITIES** You gain the following abilities as a Ghostwalker. **GHOSTWALK** You have been trained to move while attention lies elsewhere. When using the Sneak (Stealth) action, you may move up to your Speed rather than the normal distance allowed by the action. Ghostwalk does not allow you to Hide or Sneak where you lack the cover or concealment normally required to do so. **UNSEEN ASSAULT** You have learned to strike during the instant in which an enemy has lost track of you. Once per round, when you Strike a creature that is flat-footed to you as a direct result of your own Stealth, Deception or Ghostwalker abilities, you inflict an additional 1d6 precision damage. The attack must be one of the following: - An agile or finesse melee attack. - A thrown weapon attack. - A ranged weapon attack made within its first range increment. Simply flanking a creature is not sufficient to trigger Unseen Assault. The additional damage increases by 1d6 at 5th level and every 4 levels thereafter. **VANISHING RETREAT** **MOVEMENT** **Action** Reaction; **Trigger** you inflict Unseen Assault damage against a creature. You immediately Step 5 feet. This movement does not trigger reactions. **GHOST ARTS** Ghostwalkers practise specialised techniques known collectively as Ghost Arts. At 1st level, select two Ghost Arts from those described below. You learn one additional Ghost Art at 4th level and then every 4 levels thereafter. Unless specifically stated otherwise, you may only select each Ghost Art once. A Ghost Art with the Focus trait becomes expended when used and must be restored individually using Refocus (Mental Focus). Refocusing one Ghost Art does not restore any other expended Ghost Art. Some Ghost Arts are explicitly magical. Such abilities use your Ghostwalker magical tradition and Wisdom as their magical ability score. **BONUS FEATS** At 1st level you gain the Weapon Finesse feat and may select any one additional class feat. At 3rd level and then every 3 levels thereafter you may select an additional class feat. You must meet the prerequisites or match the appropriate class traits (Expert or Ghostwalker) for these feats. MAGICAL TRADITION You have no normal spellcasting progression. At 1st level, select one magical tradition. If a Ghostwalker feat or Ghost Art grants you an innate spell or explicitly magical technique without specifying its tradition, it uses your selected tradition and Wisdom as your magical ability score. The Focus trait itself remains non-magical. Mundane Ghost Arts such as Ghost Step, Smoke Veil and Spider Path cannot be detected or dispelled as magic. **GHOST ARTS** Ghost Arts are the specialised disciplines that distinguish a Ghostwalker from an ordinary infiltrator. Some rely entirely upon physical training, prepared equipment and misdirection, while others use Focus to produce effects that border upon the supernatural. Unless an art specifically states that it is magical, it is treated as a mundane technique even if its effects appear extraordinary. FALSE FACE **TECHNIQUE** You have been extensively trained in disguise, mimicry and assumed identities. You may use your Intelligence modifier instead of Charisma when making Deception checks concerned with disguising yourself or impersonating another person. Furthermore, mundane disguises that would normally require more than 1 minute to prepare may be created in 1 minute. This ability does not allow you to alter your physical body and cannot reproduce racial or supernatural features without appropriate equipment. GHOST STEP **FOCUS MOVEMENT TECHNIQUE** **Action** 1 AP You explode into sudden movement before observers can react. Stride up to your Speed. Movement made as part of Ghost Step does not trigger reactions caused by your movement. If you end this movement somewhere that provides suitable cover or concealment, you may immediately attempt to Hide as part of this action. HOLLOW BREATH **CONCENTRATE TECHNIQUE** **Action** 1 AP You slow your breathing and movement until you become unnaturally still. Until you take an action other than Awareness or Search (Perception), your breathing and other involuntary movements become almost imperceptible. Creatures relying upon sound or movement to detect you suffer a -5-circumstance penalty to their Perception checks. Furthermore, while using Hollow Breath you may hold your breath for five times the normal duration. Hollow Breath ends immediately when you move, speak, attack or perform another obvious physical action. MISDIRECTING WHISPER **FOCUS MENTAL TECHNIQUE** **Action** 1 AP You exploit a glance, gesture, whispered word or momentary distraction to draw an opponent’s attention away from your true intent. Make either a Feint or Create a Diversion check using Deception. You gain advantage on this check. After resolving the check, you may Step 5 feet. NO TRACE **TECHNIQUE** You know how to move without leaving obvious signs of your passage. Attempts to Track you using Survival are treated as one difficulty category harder than normal. When deliberately attempting to conceal your trail, you may continue moving at your normal Speed. You may still leave evidence that cannot reasonably be concealed, such as broken doors, blood, magical traces or disturbances caused by other creatures. SILENT NEEDLES **ATTACK FLOURISH FOCUS TECHNIQUE** **Action** 1 AP; **Requirements** you are wielding or carrying at least two suitable thrown weapons. You release a rapid succession of concealed weapons. Make two ranged Strikes using thrown weapons against the same creature or two different creatures. Apply your multiple attack penalty to these Strikes normally. If both attacks damage the same creature, apply DR, resistance and weakness only once. SMOKE VEIL **FOCUS MANIPULATE TECHNIQUE** **Action** 1 AP; **Range** 30 feet; **Area** 10-foot burst **Duration** 1 minute You scatter specially prepared powder, pellets or similar materials, creating a thick cloud of smoke. Creatures and objects within the area are concealed. The smoke also provides sufficient concealment for creatures within it to attempt to Hide. Strong wind, heavy rain or similar conditions may disperse the cloud early at the GM’s discretion. Smoke Veil is non-magical. SPIDER PATH **FOCUS MOVEMENT TECHNIQUE** **Action** 1 AP Through momentum, balance and specially practised footwork, you briefly treat vertical surfaces as though they were ordinary ground. Stride up to your Speed. During this movement you may travel across walls and other sufficiently solid vertical surfaces. You must finish the movement on a surface capable of supporting you. If you do not, you fall normally. Spider Path does not allow you to remain stationary on a vertical surface. FALLING SHADOW **FOCUS MOVEMENT TECHNIQUE** **Prerequisites** Level 4 **Action** R; **Trigger** you fall at least 10 feet. Through controlled rotation, wall contact and practised landing techniques, you turn a dangerous fall into little more than another avenue of escape. When calculating the damage or other consequences of the fall, treat the distance fallen as 30 feet shorter. If you land without gaining the Prone condition and your landing position provides suitable cover or concealment, you may immediately attempt to Hide (Stealth) as part of this reaction. CALTROP BLOSSOM **FOCUS MANIPULATE TECHNIQUE** **Prerequisites** Level 4 **Action** 1 AP; **Range** 20 feet; **Area** 10-foot burst You scatter a concealed handful of sharpened spikes, hooked fragments and other small impediments across the ground. The affected area becomes difficult terrain. The first time during a turn that a creature moves through the affected area using a ground movement Speed, it must make a Reflex save against your Level DC. The piercing damage is 2d6 at 4th level and increases by 1d6 at 8th level and every 4 levels thereafter. **Critical** The creature is unaffected. **Success** The creature is unaffected. **Failure** The creature takes the piercing damage and suffers a -5-foot circumstance penalty to Speed until the end of its turn. **Fumble** As failure, but the creature's movement immediately ends. The caltrops remain until removed. A creature can clear one 5-foot square using an Interact action. SHADOW DOUBLE **FOCUS SHADOW TECHNIQUE** **Prerequisites** Level 8; **Action** R; **Trigger** you are targeted by an attack that you are aware of. For a fraction of a moment, your shadow separates from you and moves in another direction, leaving your attacker uncertain which figure is real. You gain the concealed condition against the triggering attack. If the attack fails to damage you, you may immediately Step 5 feet. This movement does not trigger reactions. You remain concealed until the beginning of your next turn or until you make an attack or perform another hostile action. This Ghost Art is magical. VEILED BODY **FOCUS SHADOW TECHNIQUE** **Prerequisites** Level 8 **Action** 1 AP You suppress your presence until even the eye struggles to recognise where you stand. You become invisible until the beginning of your next turn. The effect ends immediately after you make an attack, cast a spell or take another hostile action. This Ghost Art is magical. BODY OF MIST **FOCUS SHADOW TRANSLOCATION TECHNIQUE** **Prerequisites** Level 12; **Action** 1 AP Your body briefly dissolves into a drifting cloud of shadow and vapour. You may Fly up to your Speed as part of this action. During this movement: - You may move through spaces occupied by other creatures. - You may pass through openings as narrow as 1 inch. - Your movement does not trigger reactions. - You cannot make attacks, manipulate objects or carry another creature. You cannot pass through solid walls, sealed doors or other completely enclosed barriers. You must end the movement in a space that your normal body can occupy. If you cannot, you return to the last legal space that you moved through. This Ghost Art is magical. SHADOW PASSAGE **FOCUS SHADOW TELEPORTATION TECHNIQUE** **Prerequisites** Level 12; **Action** 1 AP; **Requirements** you are within an area of dim light or darkness. Choose another location within your Speed that you can see and which is also within dim light or darkness. You disappear into the surrounding shadow and immediately appear in the chosen space. This Ghost Art is magical. EMPTY PRESENCE **FOCUS SHADOW TECHNIQUE** **Prerequisites** Level 16; **Action** 1 AP; **Duration** 1 minute You suppress not merely your appearance but the very instinct that tells another creature that someone is standing nearby. You become invisible for the duration. Unlike Veiled Body, making an attack or taking another hostile action does not end Empty Presence. Instead, immediately after resolving the hostile action you become concealed rather than invisible until the end of your current turn. At the end of your turn, if Empty Presence is still active, you become invisible again. The effect ends immediately if you become unconscious or choose to dismiss it. This Ghost Art is magical. | **GHOSTWALKER TABLE** | | | | | | | |-----------------------|---------|---------|----------|---------|----------|-----------------| | **Level** | **BAB** | **BDB** | **Fort** | **Ref** | **Will** | **Bonus Feats** | | 1st | 0 | 0 | 3 | 6 | 3 | 1 | | 2nd | 1 | 1 | 4 | 7 | 4 | 1 | | 3rd | 2 | 2 | 5 | 8 | 5 | 2 | | 4th | 3 | 3 | 6 | 9 | 6 | 2 | | 5th | 3 | 3 | 7 | 10 | 7 | 2 | | 6th | 4 | 4 | 8 | 11 | 8 | 3 | | 7th | 5 | 5 | 9 | 12 | 9 | 3 | | 8th | 6 | 6 | 10 | 13 | 10 | 3 | | 9th | 6 | 6 | 11 | 14 | 11 | 4 | | 10th | 7 | 7 | 12 | 15 | 12 | 4 | | 11th | 8 | 8 | 13 | 16 | 13 | 4 | | 12th | 9 | 9 | 14 | 17 | 14 | 5 | | 13th | 9 | 9 | 15 | 18 | 15 | 5 | | 14th | 10 | 10 | 16 | 19 | 16 | 5 | | 15th | 11 | 11 | 17 | 20 | 17 | 6 | | 16th | 12 | 12 | 18 | 21 | 18 | 6 | | 17th | 12 | 12 | 19 | 22 | 19 | 6 | | 18th | 13 | 13 | 20 | 23 | 20 | 7 | | 19th | 14 | 14 | 21 | 24 | 21 | 7 | | 20th | 15 | 15 | 22 | 25 | 22 | 7 | ## KENSAI **CLASS TYPE** Martial **DESCRIPTION** You are a disciplined master of martial technique, a warrior who has devoted their life to the perfection of weapon form and combat flow. Through rigorous training, mental clarity, and studied awareness, you have unlocked the secret language of movement—creating a unique and deadly combat rhythm. You do not simply fight. You perform a deadly dance where your blade, axe, or spear becomes an extension of thought. Unlike the brutish fury of the berserker or the tactical orders of the warlord, your strength lies in internal mastery and flawless timing. You adapt, flow, and dominate. You may want to play a Kensai if you want to excel in martial combat with intelligent control, flourish with distinctive fighting forms, and chain together devastating strikes with fluid precision. **KEY ABILITY SCORES** Dexterity (min +2), Intelligence (min +2), Constitution **PROFICIENCIES** You are proficient with all simple and martial weapons. You are proficient with all light armour, medium armour and bucklers. **CLASS SKILLS** Acrobatics, Athletics, Climbing, Culture, Handle Animal, Meditation, Mental Focus, Perception, Survival **SKILL POINTS** 4 + Int per level **HIT POINTS** 10 + Con per level **CLASS ABILITIES** You gain the following abilities as a Kensai as you advance in levels. **COMBAT FORM** **CONCENTRATE FOCUS STANCE** **Action** 1 AP You may enter a specialised stance known as a combat form. At 1st level, you begin play with two combat forms. You may select an additional combat form at 4th level and then every 4 levels thereafter. You may also gain additional combat forms by selecting the Extra Form class feat. You may only have one form active at any one time but may develop feats which allow you to modify or blend multiple forms. A full list of your available forms can be found at the end of the class description. **FLOW STRIKE** **ATTACK FLOURISH** **Action** 0 AP; Trigger you successfully hit a creature with a melee or thrown weapon You may make an additional attack against the same target. This attack is made as if it was your third strike of the turn (usually -10 but this may be lower based upon what feats you have). The attack does not count towards your MAP. **CONSIDERED MIND** Your approach to mental discipline is analytical rather than intuitive. When making Refocus (Mental Focus) checks, you may use your Intelligence modifier instead of Wisdom. **WEAPON DISCIPLINE** At 1st level, you must select one weapon group from the following: Axe, Brawling, Club, Knife, Spear, Polearm, Sword, Flail, Hammer, Pick, Dart While wielding a weapon from this group you gain the following benefits: - You add your class bonus -1 to attack and damage rolls. - The weapon gains the Finesse trait if wielded in one hand. - You are considered to have a free hand for the purpose of actions that require one (such as disarm and shove). **BONUS FEATS** At 1st level you gain the Weapon Finesse feat and any one class feat. At 3rd level and then every 3 levels thereafter you may select an additional class feat. You must meet the prerequisites or match the appropriate class traits (Martial or Kensai) for these feats. **MAGICAL TRADITION** You have no normal spellcasting progression. At 1st level select a magical tradition. If a Kensai feat grants you an innate spell or an explicitly magical technique without specifying its tradition, it uses the selected tradition and Intelligence as your magical ability score. **COMBAT FORMS** Combat Forms are specialized martial stances that shape how a Kensai fights on the battlefield. Each form emphasizes a particular combat philosophy, defence, speed, misdirection, precision, or overwhelming aggression. A form is more than a fighting technique; it is a mindset, a flow of motion and intent. While in a form, you gain unique tactical bonuses that are enhanced by your Intelligence modifier, rewarding mastery, forethought, and adaptability. Switching forms allows you to respond fluidly to changing combat conditions, and with the right feats, you can even blend or enhance these forms beyond their standard limitations. Combat Form has the Focus trait. When you activate a form, Combat Form becomes expended. You remain in the chosen form normally, but you cannot activate Combat Form again to change forms until you successfully restore the ability with Refocus. Below is the full list of known Combat Forms available to Kensai. All modifiers gained from a Combat Form are class bonus unless stated otherwise. Any triggered saving throws uses your Technique DC. **BLACK LOTUS** Graceful, poised, and lethal—this form draws from meditative precision and concealed power. When the lotus blooms, it is already too late. You conceal your true strength until the moment of impact. Whilst in this form, you gain the following modifiers: - Once per round, may delay your damage and critical rolls until the start of the enemy’s turn. - You may add your Int mod to all Feint (Deception) checks. **CRASHING TIDE** Like a tidal surge, you overwhelm enemies through relentless movement. This form teaches that power lies not in the blow, but in the rhythm that leads to it. You surge forward in rolling attacks. Whilst in this form, you gain the following modifiers: - When you move 10+ feet before attacking, gain +1 attack bonus and +Int mod to damage. - On a Critical hit, you may push the target 5 feet (Fort negates). **DREAD WOLF** You are the lone predator that picks off the weak and the unwary. The wolf does not need a pack—it thrives in the silence of fear. You isolate and dismantle lone enemies. Whilst in this form, you gain the following modifiers: - When you attack a creature not adjacent to any ally, gain +1 to attack rolls and +Int mod to damage. - When you reduce an enemy to 0 HP, gain +1 luck bonus to DB until end of next round. **ECHOING CRANE** Every motion you make reverberates with purpose. Like the crane balancing in the wind, you find strength in elegance and repetition. You fight with rhythmic grace, your movements flowing together. Whilst in this form, you gain the following modifiers: - You may add your class bonus -1 to your DB while in this form. - When you successfully avoid an attack (your DB is not overcome), you gain a +1 bonus to your next weapon attack roll this round. **EMBER REAVER** You stoke your inner fire into a storm of blades. Fuelled by momentum and fury, this form rewards ruthless aggression and constant pressure. You burn through enemies with relentless aggression. Whilst in this form, you gain the following modifiers: - If you land 2 attacks in a round, gain +Int mod secondary fire damage to the second. - Each consecutive round in this form adds +1 to weapon damage (resets if you change forms). **FLICKERING FLAME** You emulate the dancing flame—elusive, agile, and impossible to pin down. Every motion is misdirection, your steps leaving only smoke and confusion in your wake. Whilst in this form, you gain the following modifiers: - Gain a +1 bonus per 2 Int mod (min +1) to Reflex saves and Acrobatics checks. - Enemies suffer a -5 penalty to hit you with reaction attacks. **GALE CUTTER** You are the wind that howls through the battlefield, swift, erratic, and ungraspable. Each movement slices the air and your enemies alike. You dance and strike through multiple opponents. Whilst in this form, you gain the following modifiers: - Your flow strike only suffers a -5 penalty. - All attempts to grapple or restrain you are made at disadvantage (you gain advantage to resist such things). **GHOST FOX** Silent, swift, and deadly, the Ghost Fox teaches that a whisper can kill louder than a scream. You move through shadows and strike with ghostly grace. You strike from nowhere, unseen and unstoppable. Whilst in this form, you gain the following modifiers: - Add you Int mod to all Stealth skill checks. - When attacking a flat-footed target, add your Int mod as base damage **IRON TORTOISE** Like the immovable tortoise, you present a stoic defence, unyielding in the face of pressure. Your stance reflects deep inner discipline and the belief that patience can outlast fury. You adopt a defensive stance, reducing damage and holding your ground. Whilst in this form, you gain the following modifiers: - Gain +1 DB per 2 Int modifier (min +1). - All attempts to push or move you are made at disadvantage. Any saving throws that you must make to avoid being moved are made at advantage. **RISING PHOENIX** A soaring leap, a blaze of motion, this form embodies rebirth through action. You rise above your foes, crashing down with both elegance and fury. You leap into battle with furious grace. Whilst in this form, you gain the following modifiers: - Gain +2 bonus per Int mod to Climb (Climbing) and Jump (Athletics) checks. - When you Jump into melee, add +Int mod to your first attack’s damage. **STEEL VIPER** Quick as a whisper and twice as sharp, the Steel Viper strikes with refined venom. This form is about reacting faster than thought and hitting before your foe breathes. You lash out with deadly speed from deceptive angles. Whilst in this form, you gain the following modifiers: - You gain a bonus to Initiative equal to your Int mod x5. - Once per round, if you miss with an attack, roll the damage and deal it as half damage. Oathblades are warriors trained to bind action, purpose and identity together through an unbreakable personal code. HARAMAKI A haramaki, often referred to as a "belly-warmer," is a modest yet effective piece of attire. It consists of a silk sash adorned with chainmail or articulated metal plates, securely fastened around the waist to provide protection for the midsection. SHOZOKU This lightweight, dark clothing is designed for stealth and infiltration. It is completely black and covers you from head to toe. The armour provides a +2-circumstance bonus to all checks made to Hide (Stealth) when in shadowy areas. KIKKO This armour showcases a clever design, featuring hexagonal plates crafted from iron and skilfully attached to a fabric base. This arrangement grants the wearer an exceptional degree of flexibility, surpassing that offered by numerous armours with similar defensive capabilities. The wearer has the option to leave the plates visible or conceal them beneath an additional layer of fabric for added versatility. DO-MARU Among the preferred choices for martial characters seeking agility, the do-maru is the lightest of armours. This protective garment envelops the wearer's form akin to a short, armoured coat. It primarily comprises lamellar components, omitting a solid breastplate or sleeves. While this design leaves the shoulders and upper body somewhat exposed, it affords the wearer an enhanced range of motion compared to many bulkier armour options. Be aware that this armour is ineffective against critical strikes to the shoulders. KUSARI This armour is made of interlocking metal rings, offering good protection without hindering mobility. TATAMI-DO Tatami-do represents a comprehensive field armour, seamlessly merging elements of metal lamellar and kikko to form a unique suit of mail featuring a sturdy cloth backing. Typically, this armour ensemble encompasses additional components, such as a collapsible kabuto helmet or a reinforced hood, in addition to protective arm, shoulder, and thigh guards. YOROI Yoroi is a formidable combat armour, meticulously tailored with an array of supplementary elements that incorporate both plate and lamellar components. Each suit of this armour is uniquely crafted to align with its owner's aesthetic preferences. Following its construction, the armour is adorned with vivid colours and sealed with a final lacquer finish. The focal point of this armour is its cuirass, comprising two distinct sections—a dedicated reinforcement known as a waidate for the right side, and a kikko cuirass. The upper portion of the waidate features an iron plate concealed beneath leather, while the cuirass's shoulder straps, referred to as watagami, are fortified with metal plates. Further enhancements include broad lamellar shoulder guards, a kikko sleeve for the shield arm, iron greaves lacquered over padded silk leggings, and a groin protector. A defining feature of each suit is its tiered kabuto helmet, accompanied by a fearsome ho-ate mask. These masks, crafted from hardened leather or metal, often depict formidable visages such as oni, dragons, or other legendary creatures. ONI MASK These full helmets with fearsome demon masks are often worn by monastic warriors in an attempt to cow their foes. Wearing such a mask grants you a +1-item bonus to visual based Intimidate skill checks. JINGASA This conical hat is made of metal or lacquered wood, offering basic protection from head injuries. ## WEAPONS The TRG Core Rulebook provides the full rules for weapons, including weapon proficiency, damage, traits, attack penalties and the use of special combat actions. BO STAFF The bo staff, often likened to a quarterstaff, exhibits a slender and graceful design, gently tapering at one end. This versatile martial arts tool serves a dual purpose, functioning not only as a potent weapon but also as a highly effective defensive instrument. Its length and balanced construction allow martial artists to perform a wide array of techniques, making it a favoured choice for practitioners seeking agility and precision in their combat style. FIGHTING FAN Designed to mimic the elegance of a courtier's fan, this contraption is crafted from silk paper delicately stretched and folded over a folding frame constructed from hardened steel. Martial artists wield folding fans in pairs, employing a technique that expertly distracts opponents. These fans are equipped with razor-sharp tips, which can be potentially poisoned for added lethality. HANBO The hanbo is a staff-like weapon that typically measures around three feet in length, although variations can be shorter or slightly longer. The hanbo is made of wood, and its design is simple and unadorned. Due to its compact size, the hanbo is particularly suited for close-quarters combat. Its length allows for quick, precise strikes and can also be used for tripping opponents. JUTTE This baton-like weapon features a metal hook designed for blocking and pinning an opponent's weapon. Certain variants of this weapon are equipped with a sharpened metal spike or blade at the tip for added versatility and offensive capabilities. KAMA Resembling a sickle and often utilized for grain reaping in certain regions, the kama is characterized by its short, curved blade affixed to a basic wooden handle. It is occasionally known as a "kai" and is commonly wielded in pairs by martial artists skilled in its use. KATAR Punching daggers, commonly referred to as katars, are distinguished by their unique H-shaped handgrip, which enables the blade to extend from the user's knuckles. KUSIRIGAMA This unique weapon consists of a single sickle, held in the off-hand, connected to a weighted metal ball by a 10-foot length of fine chain. METEOR HAMMER This unique weapon is composed of either one or two spherical weights, each attached to a 10-foot chain. By deftly whirling the weights, you can skilfully entwine them around an opponent's body, restricting their movement and providing tactical advantages in combat. NAGINATA The naginata is a formidable weapon characterized by a 6-foot staff seamlessly joined to a 2-foot-long, slightly curved blade resembling a sword. Its well-thought-out design ensures that the wielder remains at a safe distance from opponents armed with swords and shorter weaponry, allowing for effective engagement in combat. NODACHI This formidable two-handed weapon boasts an impressive length, featuring a slender yet wickedly sharp 4-foot-long blade at one end. Predominantly employed by ground troops, it is specifically designed for launching attacks against mounted warriors, providing a strategic advantage on the battlefield. NUNCHAKU The nunchaku is a martial arts weapon comprising two sturdy wooden or metal bars that are joined together by a compact yet durable length of rope or chain. Its design allows for fluid and dynamic movements, making it a preferred choice among martial artists skilled in its artful and versatile techniques. SAI A sai is a distinctive weapon characterized by a central metal spike complemented by a pair of prongs, strategically designed for trapping an opponent's weapon. While it possesses a pointed tip, the sai is typically not employed for stabbing actions. Its primary functions involve bludgeoning adversaries, utilizing punches with the hilt, or skilfully catching and disarming weapons by leveraging the weapon's tines. Martial artists frequently wield sais in pairs, capitalizing on their formidable defensive and offensive capabilities. TETSUBO This enhanced weapon represents an improvement upon the great club, featuring a long and slender shaft. The upper half of this club is reinforced with a substantial sheet of studded iron, which not only adds weight but also provides increased strength to the weapon. TONFA These L-shaped combat sticks are well-suited for executing a dynamic blend of striking and blocking manoeuvres. The practitioner securely grips the handle and has the option to either spin the stick for offensive actions or use it to cover and reinforce the forearm for enhanced defence. WAKIZASHI These short, slender blades, measuring between 1 to 2 feet in length, serve various purposes. Powerful Fists: You know how to wield your fists as deadly weapons. The damage of your unarmed attacks is1d6 rather than the usual 1d4 inflicted by an unarmed attack. Additionally, your unarmed attacks gain the versatile bludgeoning trait.

As you become more experienced, the amount of damage that you inflict with your unarmed strikes also increases. When your BAB becomes 3 and for every 3 it increases thereafter you inflict an additional point of total unarmed damage.
Be aware that this is total unarmed damage and not base. Your base damage die still increase in the usual way.

Finally, your unarmed strikes also gain the ability to overcome various damage types as your combat prowess increases. When your BAB reaches 3, your strikes class as magical. When your BAB reaches 8 your unarmed strikes are treated as cold iron and silver and at BAB 16 they are treated as adamantine.
Disciple's Dodge: At 1st level you may add your Wisdom ability score as a dodge bonus to your Defence (DB). This bonus is only applied if you are unencumbered and wearing no armour.
Disciple's Resolve: Your training has served you well and gives you that slight edge over others. You may increase your conviction pool and conviction points by 1.
Flurry of Blows: Make two unarmed Strikes. If both hit the same creature, apply DR, resistance and weakness only once. Apply your multiple attack penalty to the Strikes normally.
Be aware that you may only inflict one critical injury when using this ability, although you still gain additional critical damage from both strikes.
Deep Focus: Your training allows you to sustain the concentration required for your techniques longer than others. Each technique you possess with the Focus trait can be used one additional time before it becomes expended and must be restored with Refocus (Mental Focus).
Each technique tracks its uses separately. When you successfully Refocus a technique, all of the uses granted to that technique by Deep Focus are restored.
Monastic Path|Disciple: As a Disciple you must select one of the Monastic Paths detailed at the end of this chapter. Your Monastic Path determines the magical tradition and magical ability score used by any innate spells or explicitly magical techniques you gain through Inner Tempest, and also grants you a class skill.
Incredible Movement: At 4<sup>th</sup> level you learn to move like the wind. You gain a +10-foot status bonus to your Speed whenever you’re not wearing armour. The bonus increases by 5 feet at 10<sup>th</sup> level and every 6 levels thereafter.
Alter the Thread: You have the ability to use your fortune and insight to great effect when avoiding harm. You may use Conviction to force an opponent to reroll an attack check against you.
Be aware that a Chaos result cannot be rerolled.
Mystical Discipline: At 1st level, you must select one of the mystical disciplines. This discipline is in addition to your Monastic Path (see below). It represents the way in which your inner discipline manifests and determines your special ability and bonus innate spells. Mystical Disciplines are explained in more detail below.
Mystical Power: Just like other adepts, you may learn to harness magic, but the spells granted by this class are innate spells rather than prepared or spontaneous spells. They follow the rules in Chapter 7 and the TRG Core Rulebook.

At 1st level you may select any two cantrips available to the magical tradition of your Monastic Path and any two spells with a base PP of 2. You gain each selected spell as an innate spell with the Focus trait. You do not memorise these spells and they cost no PP to cast. Each time you gain a level, you may add one additional eligible spell to your innate repertoire.
Be aware that an eligible spell is one from your Monastic Path's tradition whose base PP is no greater than your Mystic level.

You also gain additional innate spells from your Mystical Discipline, and you may expand your repertoire by taking the Mystic Essence feat (see Chapter 5). Each spell is tracked and Refocused separately.
Mystical Resolve: Your insight and ability to sense what is coming gives you an edge. You may increase your conviction pool and conviction points by 1.

Your Monastic Path determines the magical tradition and magical ability score of your Mystic innate spells and any explicitly magical techniques you learn, and also grants you a class skill.

Flame Within: You gain a +1-circumstance bonus to attack checks for 1 round (stacking up to +3). This resets when you end your turn without taking or dealing damage.
Inner Flame: *Ignite the soul, and all shadows burn away.*

The path of the Inner Flame is not for the timid. It calls to those whose emotions burn hot and deep—passion, anger, determination, and courage—all are fuel for the focus within. Mystics who follow this discipline have learned to stoke the fire of their soul, letting it blaze through their strikes and manifest as destructive energy. Their focus flares brightest in moments of struggle, when pain and adversity threaten to smother the spirit. But the flame never dies—it reignites, fiercer than before.

Mystics of the Inner Flame walk a dangerous edge between power and destruction, learning to burn away weakness and hesitation. In battle, they become living infernos, radiating heat, energy, and relentless force. In stillness, their hearts smoulder with a deep, controlled intensity.
You gain the Flame Within special ability.

This discipline awakens the long slumbering might of the Dragon Soul within the Mystic. Followers of this path are inspired by the timeless, sovereign power of dragons—creatures of myth who embody elemental forces and unshakable will. Through meditative communion with this primal energy, the Mystic cultivates traits of draconic dominance: unmatched presence, overwhelming breath, and inner steel.

Mystics of the Dragon Soul grow stronger with each breath drawn into their centre. Their chi becomes a vessel for elemental expression—fire, thunder, wind, or force—and their movements echo the ancient rhythm of dragonkind. To stand against them is to face not just a warrior, but a force of legend.
You gain the Dragon’s Pulse special ability.

You gain the following spells at the indicated Mystic level as innate spells with the Focus trait. These spells are in addition to any spells that you select with your class picks and don't count towards your total spells known.
Centred Awareness: **Actions** Free (0 AP); **Trigger** you make a Cleansing Trance, Clear Mind or Healing Trance check using the Meditation skill.
You gain advantage on the check.
Still Mind: *Peace is power, and in stillness, you strike true.*

Where others rush toward conflict, the Mystic of the Still Mind stands unmoved. This discipline teaches that true power comes not from the clash of bodies, but from the clarity between moments. By silencing the noise within, the Mystic hears the world more clearly anticipating attacks, resisting corruption, and acting with precise intent.

Practitioners of the Still Mind are masters of inner balance. They channel their focus to deflect distraction, purify emotion, and focus completely on the now. When chaos reigns around them, they remain serene. When others falter, they strike—cleanly, without hesitation.
You gain the Centred Awareness special ability.

You gain the following spells at the indicated Mystic level as innate spells with the Focus trait. These spells are in addition to any spells that you select with your class picks and don't count towards your total spells known.

To follow the Starborn Flow is to accept that you are part of something greater—something eternal. Mystics of this discipline surrender to the currents of fate, time, and energy that pulse through all existence. Their focus does not resist the tides of reality but rides them, allowing sudden movement, intuitive insight, and improbable escapes.

Starborn Mystics move with eerie timing, often acting just before a threat appears or just after a path opens. Their powers evoke the celestial and strange ribbons of light, pulses of gravity, bends in time. They see the patterns that others miss and move with the grace of starlight through darkness.
You gain the Echoes Beyond special ability.

Reality is not fixed—it is a hall of mirrors, and the Mystic who embraces this discipline learns to walk between the panes. The Thousand Reflections teaches that identity is fluid, action is mutable, and the self is manifold. Through focused projection and metaphysical awareness, these Mystics summon reflections of themselves, replay moments, or alter the flow of consequences.

Mystics of the Thousand Reflections are unsettling to watch. They may move in tandem with illusions, vanish before a blow lands, or act twice in the space of one heartbeat. Their combat style is disorienting and elusive, and their minds teem with divergent paths not yet taken. To them, mastery lies not in certainty—but in choice.

Reflective Mind: You instinctively throw up a reactive mental barrier which grants you advantage on the triggering saving throw.

Be aware that if you cast this spell again, any previous egg you created crumbles to ash.
Serene Defence: You enter a serene defensive stance, adding your Wisdom ability score as a dodge bonus to your DB for as long as you sustain the spell.
Timeless Motion: Time moves differently for you. You gain the quickened condition which may be used to take any action with the Movement trait each round. When taking this action your movement is imperceivable to those around you and does not provoke reactions.

description: For you, martial skill transcends the battlefield it is a lifestyle, a doctrine, and a state of mind. You search out methods of battle beyond swords and shields, finding weapons within themselves just as capable of crippling or killing as any blade. You elevate your body to be-come a weapon of war, from battle-minded ascetic to self-taught brawler. You tread the path of discipline, to discover within yourself not what you are, but what you are meant to be.

You excel at overcoming even the most daunting perils, striking where it’s least expected, and taking advantage of enemy vulnerabilities. Fleet of foot and skilled in combat, you can navigate any battlefield with ease, aiding allies wherever you are needed most.

description: Mystics follow ancient traditions of meditation, spiritual awareness and inner discipline. Many cultures describe the sensations produced by these practices as chi: a vital current linking body, mind and spirit. In rules terms, however, a Mystic does not possess a chi pool. Their extraordinary abilities are represented by techniques with the Focus trait and by innate spells.

Unlike conventional spellcasters, Mystics do not prepare spells or spend PP on the magic granted by their class. Their meditative disciplines awaken magic as an innate part of the self. These innate spells use the normal TRG Prime rules for innate magic and become expended after use when they possess the Focus trait.
